The unsafe proportion is the minimum fraction of the distance that must be moved for a collision. If no collision is detected a result of [1.0, 1.0] will be returned. Note: Any s that the shape is already colliding with e.g. inside of, will be ignored. Use [method collide_shape] to determine the s that the shape is already colliding with.

collide_shape.desc: Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a object, against the space. The resulting array contains a list of points where the shape intersects another. Like with [method intersect_shape], the number of returned results can be limited to save processing time. Returned points are a list of pairs of contact points. For each pair the first one is in the shape passed in object, second one is in the collided shape from the physics space. Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

get_rest_info.desc: Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a object, against the space. If it collides with more than one shape, the nearest one is selected. The returned object is a dictionary containing the following fields: collider_id: The colliding object's ID. linear_velocity: The colliding object's velocity . If the object is an , the result is (0, 0, 0). normal: The collision normal of the query shape at the intersection point, pointing away from the intersecting object. point: The intersection point. rid: The intersecting object's . shape: The shape index of the colliding shape. If the shape did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead. Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

intersect_point.desc: Checks whether a point is inside any solid shape. Position and other parameters are defined through . The shapes the point is inside of are returned in an array containing dictionaries with the following fields: collider: The colliding object. collider_id: The colliding object's ID. rid: The intersecting object's . shape: The shape index of the colliding shape. The number of intersections can be limited with the [param max_results] parameter, to reduce the processing time.

intersect_ray.desc: Intersects a ray in a given space. Ray position and other parameters are defined through . The returned object is a dictionary with the following fields: collider: The colliding object. collider_id: The colliding object's ID. normal: The object's surface normal at the intersection point, or Vector3(0, 0, 0) if the ray starts inside the shape and [member PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.hit_from_inside] is true. position: The intersection point. face_index: The face index at the intersection point. Note: Returns a valid number only if the intersected shape is a . Otherwise, -1 is returned. rid: The intersecting object's . shape: The shape index of the colliding shape. If the ray did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead.

intersect_shape.desc: Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a object, against the space. The intersected shapes are returned in an array containing dictionaries with the following fields: collider: The colliding object. collider_id: The colliding object's ID. rid: The intersecting object's . shape: The shape index of the colliding shape. The number of intersections can be limited with the [param max_results] parameter, to reduce the processing time. Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

PhysicsDirectSpaceState3DExtension.desc: Provides virtual methods that can be overridden to create custom implementations.

PhysicsMaterial.desc: Holds physics-related properties of a surface, namely its roughness and bounciness.

create.desc: Returns a new, pre-configured object. Use it to quickly create query parameters using the most common options. var query = PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D.create(global_position, global_position + Vector2(0, 100)) var collision = get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(query)

Returns a new, pre-configured object. Use it to quickly create query parameters using the most common options. var query = PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(position, position + Vector3(0, -10, 0)) var collision = get_world_3d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(query)

PhysicsServer2D.desc: A server interface for low-level 2D physics access.

area_add_shape.desc: Adds a shape to the area, with the given local transform. The shape (together with its [param transform] and [param disabled] properties) is added to an array of shapes, and the shapes of an area are usually referenced by their index in this array.

area_attach_canvas_instance_id.desc: Attaches the ObjectID of a canvas to the area. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the ObjectID of a .

area_attach_object_instance_id.desc: Attaches the ObjectID of an to the area. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the ObjectID of a .

area_clear_shapes.desc: Removes all shapes from the area. This does not delete the shapes themselves, so they can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later.

area_create.desc: Creates a 2D area object in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to 1, and monitorable set to false. Use [method area_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method area_set_transform] to set its transform, and use [method area_set_space] to add the area to a space. If you want the area to be detectable use [method area_set_monitorable].

area_get_canvas_instance_id.desc: Returns the ObjectID of the canvas attached to the area. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve a from a nonzero ObjectID.

area_get_collision_layer.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers the area belongs to, as a bitmask.

area_get_collision_mask.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers the area can contact with, as a bitmask.

area_get_object_instance_id.desc: Returns the ObjectID attached to the area. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve an from a nonzero ObjectID.

area_get_param.desc: Returns the value of the given area parameter.

area_get_shape.desc: Returns the of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

area_get_shape_count.desc: Returns the number of shapes added to the area.

area_get_shape_transform.desc: Returns the local transform matrix of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

area_get_space.desc: Returns the of the space assigned to the area. Returns an empty if no space is assigned.

area_get_transform.desc: Returns the transform matrix of the area.

area_remove_shape.desc: Removes the shape with the given index from the area's array of shapes. The shape itself is not deleted, so it can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later. As a result of this operation, the area's shapes which used to have indices higher than [param shape_idx] will have their index decreased by one.

area_set_area_monitor_callback.desc: Sets the area's area monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of an) area enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters: 1. an integer status: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other area's shape entered or exited the area, 2. an area_rid: the of the other area that entered or exited the area, 3. an integer instance_id: the ObjectID attached to the other area, 4. an integer area_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the other area that entered or exited the area, 5. an integer self_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the area where the other area entered or exited. By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if an area (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

area_set_collision_layer.desc: Assigns the area to one or many physics layers, via a bitmask.

area_set_collision_mask.desc: Sets which physics layers the area will monitor, via a bitmask.

area_set_monitor_callback.desc: Sets the area's body monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of a) body enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters: 1. an integer status: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other body shape entered or exited the area, 2. an body_rid: the of the body that entered or exited the area, 3. an integer instance_id: the ObjectID attached to the body, 4. an integer body_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the body that entered or exited the area, 5. an integer self_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the area where the body entered or exited. By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if a body (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

area_set_monitorable.desc: Sets whether the area is monitorable or not. If [param monitorable] is true, the area monitoring callback of other areas will be called when this area enters or exits them.

area_set_param.desc: Sets the value of the given area parameter.

area_set_shape.desc: Replaces the area's shape at the given index by another shape, while not affecting the transform and disabled properties at the same index.

area_set_shape_disabled.desc: Sets the disabled property of the area's shape with the given index. If [param disabled] is true, then the shape will not detect any other shapes entering or exiting it.

area_set_shape_transform.desc: Sets the local transform matrix of the area's shape with the given index.

area_set_space.desc: Adds the area to the given space, after removing the area from the previously assigned space (if any). Note: To remove an area from a space without immediately adding it back elsewhere, use PhysicsServer2D.area_set_space(area, RID()).

area_set_transform.desc: Sets the transform matrix of the area.

body_add_collision_exception.desc: Adds [param excepted_body] to the body's list of collision exceptions, so that collisions with it are ignored.

body_add_constant_central_force.desc: Adds a constant directional force to the body. The force does not affect rotation. The force remains applied over time until cleared with PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_force(body, Vector2(0, 0)). This is equivalent to using [method body_add_constant_force] at the body's center of mass.

body_add_constant_force.desc: Adds a constant positioned force to the body. The force can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass. The force remains applied over time until cleared with PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_force(body, Vector2(0, 0)). [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_add_constant_torque.desc: Adds a constant rotational force to the body. The force does not affect position. The force remains applied over time until cleared with PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_torque(body, 0).

body_add_shape.desc: Adds a shape to the area, with the given local transform. The shape (together with its [param transform] and [param disabled] properties) is added to an array of shapes, and the shapes of a body are usually referenced by their index in this array.

body_apply_central_force.desc: Applies a directional force to the body, at the body's center of mass. The force does not affect rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update. This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_force] at the body's center of mass.

body_apply_central_impulse.desc: Applies a directional impulse to the body, at the body's center of mass. The impulse does not affect rotation. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise). This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_impulse] at the body's center of mass.

body_apply_force.desc: Applies a positioned force to the body. The force can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update. [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_apply_impulse.desc: Applies a positioned impulse to the body. The impulse can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise). [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_apply_torque.desc: Applies a rotational force to the body. The force does not affect position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

body_apply_torque_impulse.desc: Applies a rotational impulse to the body. The impulse does not affect position. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

body_attach_canvas_instance_id.desc: Attaches the ObjectID of a canvas to the body. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the ObjectID of a .

body_attach_object_instance_id.desc: Attaches the ObjectID of an to the body. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the ObjectID of a .

body_clear_shapes.desc: Removes all shapes from the body. This does not delete the shapes themselves, so they can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later.

body_create.desc: Creates a 2D body object in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to 1, and body mode set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID]. Use [method body_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method body_set_state] to set its transform, and use [method body_set_space] to add the body to a space.

body_get_canvas_instance_id.desc: Returns the ObjectID of the canvas attached to the body. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve a from a nonzero ObjectID.

body_get_collision_layer.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers the body belongs to, as a bitmask.

body_get_collision_mask.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers the body can collide with, as a bitmask.

body_get_collision_priority.desc: Returns the body's collision priority. This is used in the depenetration phase of [method body_test_motion]. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the body will be.

body_get_constant_force.desc: Returns the body's total constant positional force applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

body_get_constant_torque.desc: Returns the body's total constant rotational force applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_torque].

body_get_continuous_collision_detection_.desc: Returns the body's continuous collision detection mode.

body_get_direct_state.desc: Returns the of the body. Returns null if the body is destroyed or not assigned to a space.

body_get_max_contacts_reported.desc: Returns the maximum number of contacts that the body can report. See [method body_set_max_contacts_reported].

body_get_object_instance_id.desc: Returns the ObjectID attached to the body. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve an from a nonzero ObjectID.

body_get_param.desc: Returns the value of the given body parameter.

body_get_shape.desc: Returns the of the shape with the given index in the body's array of shapes.

body_get_shape_count.desc: Returns the number of shapes added to the body.

body_get_shape_transform.desc: Returns the local transform matrix of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

body_get_space.desc: Returns the of the space assigned to the body. Returns an empty if no space is assigned.

body_get_state.desc: Returns the value of the given state of the body.

body_is_omitting_force_integration.desc: Returns true if the body is omitting the standard force integration. See [method body_set_omit_force_integration].

body_remove_collision_exception.desc: Removes [param excepted_body] from the body's list of collision exceptions, so that collisions with it are no longer ignored.

body_remove_shape.desc: Removes the shape with the given index from the body's array of shapes. The shape itself is not deleted, so it can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later. As a result of this operation, the body's shapes which used to have indices higher than [param shape_idx] will have their index decreased by one.

body_reset_mass_properties.desc: Restores the default inertia and center of mass of the body based on its shapes. This undoes any custom values previously set using [method body_set_param].

body_set_axis_velocity.desc: Modifies the body's linear velocity so that its projection to the axis axis_velocity.normalized() is exactly axis_velocity.length(). This is useful for jumping behavior.

body_set_collision_layer.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers the body belongs to, via a bitmask.

body_set_collision_mask.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers the body can collide with, via a bitmask.

body_set_collision_priority.desc: Sets the body's collision priority. This is used in the depenetration phase of [method body_test_motion]. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the body will be.

body_set_constant_force.desc: Sets the body's total constant positional force applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

body_set_constant_torque.desc: Sets the body's total constant rotational force applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_torque].

body_set_continuous_collision_detection_.desc: Sets the continuous collision detection mode. Continuous collision detection tries to predict where a moving body would collide in between physics updates, instead of moving it and correcting its movement if it collided.

body_set_force_integration_callback.desc: Sets the body's custom force integration callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty ([code skip-lint]Callable()) to clear the custom callback. The function [param callable] will be called every physics tick, before the standard force integration (see [method body_set_omit_force_integration]). It can be used for example to update the body's linear and angular velocity based on contact with other bodies. If [param userdata] is not null, the function [param callable] must take the following two parameters: 1. state: a used to retrieve and modify the body's state, 2. [code skip-lint]userdata: a ; its value will be the [param userdata] passed into this method. If [param userdata] is null, then [param callable] must take only the state parameter.

body_set_max_contacts_reported.desc: Sets the maximum number of contacts that the body can report. If [param amount] is greater than zero, then the body will keep track of at most this many contacts with other bodies.

body_set_omit_force_integration.desc: Sets whether the body omits the standard force integration. If [param enable] is true, the body will not automatically use applied forces, torques, and damping to update the body's linear and angular velocity. In this case, [method body_set_force_integration_callback] can be used to manually update the linear and angular velocity instead. This method is called when the property [member RigidBody2D.custom_integrator] is set.

body_set_param.desc: Sets the value of the given body parameter.

body_set_shape.desc: Replaces the body's shape at the given index by another shape, while not affecting the transform, disabled, and one-way collision properties at the same index.

body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision.desc: Sets the one-way collision properties of the body's shape with the given index. If [param enable] is true, the one-way collision direction given by the shape's local upward axis body_get_shape_transform(body, shape_idx).y will be used to ignore collisions with the shape in the opposite direction, and to ensure depenetration of kinematic bodies happens in this direction.

body_set_shape_disabled.desc: Sets the disabled property of the body's shape with the given index. If [param disabled] is true, then the shape will be ignored in all collision detection.

body_set_shape_transform.desc: Sets the local transform matrix of the body's shape with the given index.

body_set_space.desc: Adds the body to the given space, after removing the body from the previously assigned space (if any). If the body's mode is set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID], then adding the body to a space will have the following additional effects: - If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_CENTER_OF_MASS] has never been set explicitly, then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes. - If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_INERTIA] is set to a value <= 0.0, then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes, mass, and center of mass. Note: To remove a body from a space without immediately adding it back elsewhere, use PhysicsServer2D.body_set_space(body, RID()).

body_set_state.desc: Sets the value of a body's state. Note: The state change doesn't take effect immediately. The state will change on the next physics frame.

body_set_state_sync_callback.desc: Sets the body's state synchronization callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty ([code skip-lint]Callable()) to clear the callback. The function [param callable] will be called every physics frame, assuming that the body was active during the previous physics tick, and can be used to fetch the latest state from the physics server. The function [param callable] must take the following parameters: 1. state: a , used to retrieve the body's state.

body_test_motion.desc: Returns true if a collision would result from moving the body along a motion vector from a given point in space. See for the available motion parameters. Optionally a object can be passed, which will be used to store the information about the resulting collision.

capsule_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D capsule shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the capsule's height and radius.

circle_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D circle shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the circle's radius.

concave_polygon_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D concave polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the concave polygon's segments.

convex_polygon_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D convex polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the convex polygon's points.

damped_spring_joint_get_param.desc: Returns the value of the given damped spring joint parameter.

damped_spring_joint_set_param.desc: Sets the value of the given damped spring joint parameter.

free_rid.desc: Destroys any of the objects created by PhysicsServer2D. If the passed is not one of the objects that can be created by PhysicsServer2D, an error will be printed to the console.

get_process_info.desc: Returns the value of a physics engine state specified by [param process_info].

joint_clear.desc: Destroys the joint with the given , creates a new uninitialized joint, and makes the refer to this new joint.

joint_create.desc: Creates a 2D joint in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. To set the joint type, use [method joint_make_damped_spring], [method joint_make_groove] or [method joint_make_pin]. Use [method joint_set_param] to set generic joint parameters.

joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies.desc: Sets whether the bodies attached to the will collide with each other.

joint_get_param.desc: Returns the value of the given joint parameter.

joint_is_disabled_collisions_between_bod.desc: Returns whether the bodies attached to the will collide with each other.

joint_make_damped_spring.desc: Makes the joint a damped spring joint, attached at the point [param anchor_a] (given in global coordinates) on the body [param body_a] and at the point [param anchor_b] (given in global coordinates) on the body [param body_b]. To set the parameters which are specific to the damped spring, see [method damped_spring_joint_set_param].

joint_make_groove.desc: Makes the joint a groove joint.

joint_make_pin.desc: Makes the joint a pin joint. If [param body_b] is an empty , then [param body_a] is pinned to the point [param anchor] (given in global coordinates); otherwise, [param body_a] is pinned to [param body_b] at the point [param anchor] (given in global coordinates). To set the parameters which are specific to the pin joint, see [method pin_joint_set_param].

joint_set_param.desc: Sets the value of the given joint parameter.

pin_joint_get_param.desc: Returns the value of a pin joint parameter.

rectangle_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D rectangle shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the rectangle's half-extents.

segment_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D segment shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the segment's start and end points.

separation_ray_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D separation ray shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's length and slide_on_slope properties.

set_active.desc: Activates or deactivates the 2D physics server. If [param active] is false, then the physics server will not do anything in its physics step.

shape_get_data.desc: Returns the shape data that defines the configuration of the shape, such as the half-extents of a rectangle or the segments of a concave shape. See [method shape_set_data] for the precise format of this data in each case.

shape_set_data.desc: Sets the shape data that defines the configuration of the shape. The [param data] to be passed depends on the shape's type (see [method shape_get_type]): - [constant SHAPE_WORLD_BOUNDARY]: an array of length two containing a normal direction and a distance d, - [constant SHAPE_SEPARATION_RAY]: a dictionary containing the key length with a value and the key slide_on_slope with a value, - [constant SHAPE_SEGMENT]: a rect containing the first point of the segment in rect.position and the second point of the segment in rect.size, - [constant SHAPE_CIRCLE]: a radius, - [constant SHAPE_RECTANGLE]: a half_extents, - [constant SHAPE_CAPSULE]: an array of length two (or a ) containing a height and a radius, - [constant SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON]: either a of points defining a convex polygon in counterclockwise order (the clockwise outward normal of each segment formed by consecutive points is calculated internally), or a of length divisible by four so that every 4-tuple of s contains the coordinates of a point followed by the coordinates of the clockwise outward normal vector to the segment between the current point and the next point, - [constant SHAPE_CONCAVE_POLYGON]: a of length divisible by two (each pair of points forms one segment). Warning: In the case of [constant SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON], this method does not check if the points supplied actually form a convex polygon (unlike the [member CollisionPolygon2D.polygon] property).

space_create.desc: Creates a 2D space in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. A space contains bodies and areas, and controls the stepping of the physics simulation of the objects in it.

space_get_direct_state.desc: Returns the state of a space, a . This object can be used for collision/intersection queries.

space_get_param.desc: Returns the value of the given space parameter.

space_is_active.desc: Returns true if the space is active.

space_set_active.desc: Activates or deactivates the space. If [param active] is false, then the physics server will not do anything with this space in its physics step.

space_set_param.desc: Sets the value of the given space parameter.

world_boundary_shape_create.desc: Creates a 2D world boundary shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's normal direction and distance properties.

PhysicsServer2DExtension.desc: Provides virtual methods that can be overridden to create custom implementations.

_area_set_pickable.desc: If set to true, allows the area with the given to detect mouse inputs when the mouse cursor is hovering on it. Overridable version of 's internal area_set_pickable method. Corresponds to [member CollisionObject2D.input_pickable].

_body_collide_shape.desc: Given a [param body], a [param shape], and their respective parameters, this method should return true if a collision between the two would occur, with additional details passed in [param results]. Overridable version of 's internal shape_collide method. Corresponds to [method PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.collide_shape].

_body_get_collision_exceptions.desc: Returns the s of all bodies added as collision exceptions for the given [param body]. See also [method _body_add_collision_exception] and [method _body_remove_collision_exception]. Overridable version of 's internal body_get_collision_exceptions method. Corresponds to [method PhysicsBody2D.get_collision_exceptions].

_body_get_contacts_reported_depth_thresh.desc: Overridable version of 's internal body_get_contacts_reported_depth_threshold method. Note: This method is currently unused by Godot's default physics implementation.

_body_set_contacts_reported_depth_thresh.desc: Overridable version of 's internal body_set_contacts_reported_depth_threshold method. Note: This method is currently unused by Godot's default physics implementation.

_body_set_pickable.desc: If set to true, allows the body with the given to detect mouse inputs when the mouse cursor is hovering on it. Overridable version of 's internal body_set_pickable method. Corresponds to [member CollisionObject2D.input_pickable].

_body_set_state_sync_callback.desc: Assigns the [param body] to call the given [param callable] during the synchronization phase of the loop, before [method _step] is called. See also [method _sync]. Overridable version of [method PhysicsServer2D.body_set_state_sync_callback].

_body_test_motion.desc: Overridable version of [method PhysicsServer2D.body_test_motion]. Unlike the exposed implementation, this method does not receive all of the arguments inside a .

_end_sync.desc: Called to indicate that the physics server has stopped synchronizing. It is in the loop's iteration/physics phase, and can access physics objects even if running on a separate thread. See also [method _sync]. Overridable version of 's internal end_sync method.

_finish.desc: Called when the main loop finalizes to shut down the physics server. See also [method MainLoop._finalize] and [method _init]. Overridable version of 's internal finish method.

_flush_queries.desc: Called every physics step before [method _step] to process all remaining queries. Overridable version of 's internal flush_queries method.

_init.desc: Called when the main loop is initialized and creates a new instance of this physics server. See also [method MainLoop._initialize] and [method _finish]. Overridable version of 's internal init method.

_is_flushing_queries.desc: Overridable method that should return true when the physics server is processing queries. See also [method _flush_queries]. Overridable version of 's internal is_flushing_queries method.

_shape_collide.desc: Given two shapes and their parameters, should return true if a collision between the two would occur, with additional details passed in [param results]. Overridable version of 's internal shape_collide method. Corresponds to [method PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.collide_shape].

_shape_get_custom_solver_bias.desc: Should return the custom solver bias of the given [param shape], which defines how much bodies are forced to separate on contact when this shape is involved. Overridable version of 's internal shape_get_custom_solver_bias method. Corresponds to [member Shape2D.custom_solver_bias].

_shape_set_custom_solver_bias.desc: Should set the custom solver bias for the given [param shape]. It defines how much bodies are forced to separate on contact. Overridable version of 's internal shape_get_custom_solver_bias method. Corresponds to [member Shape2D.custom_solver_bias].

_space_get_contact_count.desc: Should return how many contacts have occurred during the last physics step in the given [param space]. See also [method _space_get_contacts] and [method _space_set_debug_contacts]. Overridable version of 's internal space_get_contact_count method.

_space_get_contacts.desc: Should return the positions of all contacts that have occurred during the last physics step in the given [param space]. See also [method _space_get_contact_count] and [method _space_set_debug_contacts]. Overridable version of 's internal space_get_contacts method.

_space_set_debug_contacts.desc: Used internally to allow the given [param space] to store contact points, up to [param max_contacts]. This is automatically set for the main 's space when [member SceneTree.debug_collisions_hint] is true, or by checking "Visible Collision Shapes" in the editor. Only works in debug builds. Overridable version of 's internal space_set_debug_contacts method.

_step.desc: Called every physics step to process the physics simulation. [param step] is the time elapsed since the last physics step, in seconds. It is usually the same as the value returned by [method Node.get_physics_process_delta_time]. Overridable version of 's internal [code skip-lint]step method.

_sync.desc: Called to indicate that the physics server is synchronizing and cannot access physics states if running on a separate thread. See also [method _end_sync]. Overridable version of 's internal sync method.

body_test_motion_is_excluding_body.desc: Returns true if the body with the given is being excluded from [method _body_test_motion]. See also [method Object.get_instance_id].

body_test_motion_is_excluding_object.desc: Returns true if the object with the given instance ID is being excluded from [method _body_test_motion]. See also [method Object.get_instance_id].

register_server.desc: Register a implementation by passing a [param name] and a that returns a object.

set_default_server.desc: Set the default implementation to the one identified by [param name], if [param priority] is greater than the priority of the current default implementation.

PhysicsServer3D.desc: A server interface for low-level 3D physics access.

area_add_shape.desc: Adds a shape to the area, along with a transform matrix. Shapes are usually referenced by their index, so you should track which shape has a given index.

area_attach_object_instance_id.desc: Assigns the area to a descendant of , so it can exist in the node tree.

area_clear_shapes.desc: Removes all shapes from an area. It does not delete the shapes, so they can be reassigned later.

area_create.desc: Creates a 3D area object in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to 1, and monitorable set to false. Use [method area_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method area_set_transform] to set its transform, and use [method area_set_space] to add the area to a space. If you want the area to be detectable use [method area_set_monitorable].

area_get_collision_layer.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers an area belongs to.

area_get_collision_mask.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers an area can contact with.

area_get_object_instance_id.desc: Gets the instance ID of the object the area is assigned to.

area_get_param.desc: Returns an area parameter value. A list of available parameters is on the [enum AreaParameter] constants.

area_get_shape.desc: Returns the of the nth shape of an area.

area_get_shape_count.desc: Returns the number of shapes assigned to an area.

area_get_shape_transform.desc: Returns the transform matrix of a shape within an area.

area_get_space.desc: Returns the space assigned to the area.

area_get_transform.desc: Returns the transform matrix for an area.

area_remove_shape.desc: Removes a shape from an area. It does not delete the shape, so it can be reassigned later.

area_set_area_monitor_callback.desc: Sets the area's area monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of an) area enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters: 1. an integer status: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other area's shape entered or exited the area, 2. an area_rid: the of the other area that entered or exited the area, 3. an integer instance_id: the ObjectID attached to the other area, 4. an integer area_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the other area that entered or exited the area, 5. an integer self_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the area where the other area entered or exited. By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if an area (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

area_set_collision_layer.desc: Assigns the area to one or many physics layers.

area_set_collision_mask.desc: Sets which physics layers the area will monitor.

area_set_monitor_callback.desc: Sets the area's body monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of a) body enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters: 1. an integer status: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other body shape entered or exited the area, 2. an body_rid: the of the body that entered or exited the area, 3. an integer instance_id: the ObjectID attached to the body, 4. an integer body_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the body that entered or exited the area, 5. an integer self_shape_idx: the index of the shape of the area where the body entered or exited. By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if a body (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

area_set_param.desc: Sets the value for an area parameter. A list of available parameters is on the [enum AreaParameter] constants.

area_set_shape.desc: Substitutes a given area shape by another. The old shape is selected by its index, the new one by its .

area_set_shape_transform.desc: Sets the transform matrix for an area shape.

area_set_space.desc: Assigns a space to the area.

area_set_transform.desc: Sets the transform matrix for an area.

body_add_collision_exception.desc: Adds a body to the list of bodies exempt from collisions.

body_add_constant_central_force.desc: Adds a constant directional force without affecting rotation that keeps being applied over time until cleared with body_set_constant_force(body, Vector3(0, 0, 0)). This is equivalent to using [method body_add_constant_force] at the body's center of mass.

body_add_constant_force.desc: Adds a constant positioned force to the body that keeps being applied over time until cleared with body_set_constant_force(body, Vector3(0, 0, 0)). [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_add_constant_torque.desc: Adds a constant rotational force without affecting position that keeps being applied over time until cleared with body_set_constant_torque(body, Vector3(0, 0, 0)).

body_add_shape.desc: Adds a shape to the body, along with a transform matrix. Shapes are usually referenced by their index, so you should track which shape has a given index.

body_apply_central_force.desc: Applies a directional force without affecting rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update. This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_force] at the body's center of mass.

body_apply_central_impulse.desc: Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise). This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_impulse] at the body's center of mass.

body_apply_force.desc: Applies a positioned force to the body. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update. [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_apply_impulse.desc: Applies a positioned impulse to the body. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise). [param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

body_apply_torque.desc: Applies a rotational force without affecting position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

body_apply_torque_impulse.desc: Applies a rotational impulse to the body without affecting the position. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

body_attach_object_instance_id.desc: Assigns the area to a descendant of , so it can exist in the node tree.

body_clear_shapes.desc: Removes all shapes from a body.

body_create.desc: Creates a 3D body object in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to 1, and body mode set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID]. Use [method body_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method body_set_state] to set its transform, and use [method body_set_space] to add the body to a space.

body_get_collision_layer.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers a body belongs to.

body_get_collision_mask.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers a body can collide with.

body_get_constant_force.desc: Returns the body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

body_get_constant_torque.desc: Returns the body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_torque].

body_get_direct_state.desc: Returns the of the body. Returns null if the body is destroyed or removed from the physics space.

body_get_max_contacts_reported.desc: Returns the maximum contacts that can be reported. See [method body_set_max_contacts_reported].

body_get_object_instance_id.desc: Gets the instance ID of the object the area is assigned to.

body_get_param.desc: Returns the value of a body parameter. A list of available parameters is on the [enum BodyParameter] constants.

body_get_shape.desc: Returns the of the nth shape of a body.

body_get_shape_count.desc: Returns the number of shapes assigned to a body.

body_get_shape_transform.desc: Returns the transform matrix of a body shape.

body_get_space.desc: Returns the of the space assigned to a body.

body_is_continuous_collision_detection_e.desc: If true, the continuous collision detection mode is enabled.

body_is_omitting_force_integration.desc: Returns true if the body is omitting the standard force integration. See [method body_set_omit_force_integration].

body_remove_collision_exception.desc: Removes a body from the list of bodies exempt from collisions. Continuous collision detection tries to predict where a moving body will collide, instead of moving it and correcting its movement if it collided.

body_remove_shape.desc: Removes a shape from a body. The shape is not deleted, so it can be reused afterwards.

body_reset_mass_properties.desc: Restores the default inertia and center of mass based on shapes to cancel any custom values previously set using [method body_set_param].

body_set_axis_velocity.desc: Sets an axis velocity. The velocity in the given vector axis will be set as the given vector length. This is useful for jumping behavior.

body_set_collision_layer.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers a body belongs to.

body_set_collision_mask.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers a body can collide with.

body_set_constant_force.desc: Sets the body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

body_set_constant_torque.desc: Sets the body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update. See [method body_add_constant_torque].

body_set_enable_continuous_collision_det.desc: If true, the continuous collision detection mode is enabled. Continuous collision detection tries to predict where a moving body will collide, instead of moving it and correcting its movement if it collided.

body_set_force_integration_callback.desc: Sets the body's custom force integration callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty ([code skip-lint]Callable()) to clear the custom callback. The function [param callable] will be called every physics tick, before the standard force integration (see [method body_set_omit_force_integration]). It can be used for example to update the body's linear and angular velocity based on contact with other bodies. If [param userdata] is not null, the function [param callable] must take the following two parameters: 1. state: a , used to retrieve and modify the body's state, 2. [code skip-lint]userdata: a ; its value will be the [param userdata] passed into this method. If [param userdata] is null, then [param callable] must take only the state parameter.

body_set_max_contacts_reported.desc: Sets the maximum contacts to report. Bodies can keep a log of the contacts with other bodies. This is enabled by setting the maximum number of contacts reported to a number greater than 0.

body_set_omit_force_integration.desc: Sets whether the body omits the standard force integration. If [param enable] is true, the body will not automatically use applied forces, torques, and damping to update the body's linear and angular velocity. In this case, [method body_set_force_integration_callback] can be used to manually update the linear and angular velocity instead. This method is called when the property [member RigidBody3D.custom_integrator] is set.

body_set_param.desc: Sets a body parameter. A list of available parameters is on the [enum BodyParameter] constants.

body_set_ray_pickable.desc: Sets the body pickable with rays if [param enable] is set.

body_set_shape.desc: Substitutes a given body shape by another. The old shape is selected by its index, the new one by its .

body_set_shape_transform.desc: Sets the transform matrix for a body shape.

body_set_space.desc: Assigns a space to the body (see [method space_create]).

body_set_state_sync_callback.desc: Sets the body's state synchronization callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty ([code skip-lint]Callable()) to clear the callback. The function [param callable] will be called every physics frame, assuming that the body was active during the previous physics tick, and can be used to fetch the latest state from the physics server. The function [param callable] must take the following parameters: 1. state: a , used to retrieve the body's state.

body_test_motion.desc: Returns true if a collision would result from moving along a motion vector from a given point in space. is passed to set motion parameters. can be passed to return additional information.

box_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D box shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the box's half-extents.

capsule_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D capsule shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the capsule's height and radius.

concave_polygon_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D concave polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the concave polygon's triangles.

cone_twist_joint_get_param.desc: Gets a cone twist joint parameter.

cone_twist_joint_set_param.desc: Sets a cone twist joint parameter.

convex_polygon_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D convex polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the convex polygon's points.

custom_shape_create.desc: Creates a custom shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's data. Note: Custom shapes are not supported by the built-in physics servers, so calling this method always produces an error when using Godot Physics or Jolt Physics. Custom physics servers implemented as GDExtensions may support a custom shape.

cylinder_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D cylinder shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the cylinder's height and radius.

free_rid.desc: Destroys any of the objects created by PhysicsServer3D. If the passed is not one of the objects that can be created by PhysicsServer3D, an error will be sent to the console.

generic_6dof_joint_get_flag.desc: Returns the value of a generic 6DOF joint flag.

generic_6dof_joint_get_param.desc: Returns the value of a generic 6DOF joint parameter.

generic_6dof_joint_set_flag.desc: Sets the value of a given generic 6DOF joint flag.

generic_6dof_joint_set_param.desc: Sets the value of a given generic 6DOF joint parameter.

get_process_info.desc: Returns the value of a physics engine state specified by [param process_info].

heightmap_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D heightmap shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the heightmap's data.

joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies.desc: Sets whether the bodies attached to the will collide with each other.

joint_get_solver_priority.desc: Gets the priority value of the Joint3D.

joint_get_type.desc: Returns the type of the Joint3D.

joint_is_disabled_collisions_between_bod.desc: Returns whether the bodies attached to the will collide with each other.

joint_make_generic_6dof.desc: Make the joint a generic six degrees of freedom (6DOF) joint. Use [method generic_6dof_joint_set_flag] and [method generic_6dof_joint_set_param] to set the joint's flags and parameters respectively.

joint_set_solver_priority.desc: Sets the priority value of the Joint3D.

pin_joint_get_local_a.desc: Returns position of the joint in the local space of body a of the joint.

pin_joint_get_local_b.desc: Returns position of the joint in the local space of body b of the joint.

pin_joint_set_local_a.desc: Sets position of the joint in the local space of body a of the joint.

pin_joint_set_local_b.desc: Sets position of the joint in the local space of body b of the joint.

separation_ray_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D separation ray shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's length and slide_on_slope properties.

set_active.desc: Activates or deactivates the 3D physics engine.

shape_get_data.desc: Returns the shape data that configures the shape, such as the half-extents of a box or the triangles of a concave (trimesh) shape. See [method shape_set_data] for the precise format of this data in each case.

shape_get_margin.desc: Returns the collision margin for the shape. Note: This is not used in Godot Physics, so will always return 0.

shape_set_data.desc: Sets the shape data that configures the shape. The [param data] to be passed depends on the shape's type (see [method shape_get_type]): - [constant SHAPE_WORLD_BOUNDARY]: a , - [constant SHAPE_SEPARATION_RAY]: a dictionary containing the key "length" with a value and the key "slide_on_slope" with a value, - [constant SHAPE_SPHERE]: a that is the radius of the sphere, - [constant SHAPE_BOX]: a containing the half-extents of the box, - [constant SHAPE_CAPSULE]: a dictionary containing the keys "height" and "radius" with values, - [constant SHAPE_CYLINDER]: a dictionary containing the keys "height" and "radius" with values, - [constant SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON]: a of points defining a convex polygon (the shape will be the convex hull of the points), - [constant SHAPE_CONCAVE_POLYGON]: a dictionary containing the key "faces" with a value (with a length divisible by 3, so that each 3-tuple of points forms a face) and the key "backface_collision" with a value, - [constant SHAPE_HEIGHTMAP]: a dictionary containing the keys "width" and "depth" with values, and the key "heights" with a value that is a packed array of s of length width * depth (that is a , or a if Godot was compiled with the precision=double option), and optionally the keys "min_height" and "max_height" with values, - [constant SHAPE_SOFT_BODY]: the input [param data] is ignored and this method has no effect, - [constant SHAPE_CUSTOM]: the input [param data] is interpreted by a custom physics server, if it supports custom shapes.

shape_set_margin.desc: Sets the collision margin for the shape. Note: This is not used in Godot Physics.

soft_body_add_collision_exception.desc: Adds the given body to the list of bodies exempt from collisions.

soft_body_apply_central_force.desc: Distributes and applies a force to all points. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

soft_body_apply_central_impulse.desc: Distributes and applies an impulse to all points. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

soft_body_apply_point_force.desc: Applies a force to a point. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

soft_body_apply_point_impulse.desc: Applies an impulse to a point. An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

soft_body_create.desc: Creates a new soft body and returns its internal .

soft_body_get_bounds.desc: Returns the bounds of the given soft body in global coordinates.

soft_body_get_collision_layer.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers that the given soft body belongs to.

soft_body_get_collision_mask.desc: Returns the physics layer or layers that the given soft body can collide with.

soft_body_get_damping_coefficient.desc: Returns the damping coefficient of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_drag_coefficient.desc: Returns the drag coefficient of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_linear_stiffness.desc: Returns the linear stiffness of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_point_global_position.desc: Returns the current position of the given soft body point in global coordinates.

soft_body_get_pressure_coefficient.desc: Returns the pressure coefficient of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_shrinking_factor.desc: Returns the shrinking factor of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_simulation_precision.desc: Returns the simulation precision of the given soft body.

soft_body_get_space.desc: Returns the of the space assigned to the given soft body.

soft_body_get_state.desc: Returns the given soft body state. Note: Godot's default physics implementation does not support [constant BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY], [constant BODY_STATE_ANGULAR_VELOCITY], [constant BODY_STATE_SLEEPING], or [constant BODY_STATE_CAN_SLEEP].

soft_body_get_total_mass.desc: Returns the total mass assigned to the given soft body.

soft_body_is_point_pinned.desc: Returns whether the given soft body point is pinned.

soft_body_move_point.desc: Moves the given soft body point to a position in global coordinates.

soft_body_pin_point.desc: Pins or unpins the given soft body point based on the value of [param pin]. Note: Pinning a point effectively makes it kinematic, preventing it from being affected by forces, but you can still move it using [method soft_body_move_point].

soft_body_remove_all_pinned_points.desc: Unpins all points of the given soft body.

soft_body_remove_collision_exception.desc: Removes the given body from the list of bodies exempt from collisions.

soft_body_set_collision_layer.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers the given soft body belongs to.

soft_body_set_collision_mask.desc: Sets the physics layer or layers the given soft body can collide with.

soft_body_set_damping_coefficient.desc: Sets the damping coefficient of the given soft body. Higher values will slow down the body more noticeably when forces are applied.

soft_body_set_drag_coefficient.desc: Sets the drag coefficient of the given soft body. Higher values increase this body's air resistance. Note: This value is currently unused by Godot's default physics implementation.

soft_body_set_linear_stiffness.desc: Sets the linear stiffness of the given soft body. Higher values will result in a stiffer body, while lower values will increase the body's ability to bend. The value can be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).

soft_body_set_mesh.desc: Sets the mesh of the given soft body.

soft_body_set_pressure_coefficient.desc: Sets the pressure coefficient of the given soft body. Simulates pressure build-up from inside this body. Higher values increase the strength of this effect.

soft_body_set_ray_pickable.desc: Sets whether the given soft body will be pickable when using object picking.

soft_body_set_shrinking_factor.desc: Sets the shrinking factor of the given soft body.

soft_body_set_simulation_precision.desc: Sets the simulation precision of the given soft body. Increasing this value will improve the resulting simulation, but can affect performance. Use with care.

soft_body_set_space.desc: Assigns a space to the given soft body (see [method space_create]).

soft_body_set_state.desc: Sets the given body state for the given body. Note: Godot's default physics implementation does not support [constant BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY], [constant BODY_STATE_ANGULAR_VELOCITY], [constant BODY_STATE_SLEEPING], or [constant BODY_STATE_CAN_SLEEP].

soft_body_set_total_mass.desc: Sets the total mass for the given soft body.

soft_body_set_transform.desc: Sets the global transform of the given soft body.

soft_body_update_rendering_server.desc: Requests that the physics server updates the rendering server with the latest positions of the given soft body's points through the [param rendering_server_handler] interface.

space_create.desc: Creates a space. A space is a collection of parameters for the physics engine that can be assigned to an area or a body. It can be assigned to an area with [method area_set_space], or to a body with [method body_set_space].

space_get_direct_state.desc: Returns the state of a space, a . This object can be used to make collision/intersection queries.

space_get_param.desc: Returns the value of a space parameter.

space_is_active.desc: Returns whether the space is active.

space_set_active.desc: Marks a space as active. It will not have an effect, unless it is assigned to an area or body.

space_set_param.desc: Sets the value for a space parameter. A list of available parameters is on the [enum SpaceParameter] constants.

sphere_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D sphere shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the sphere's radius.

world_boundary_shape_create.desc: Creates a 3D world boundary shape in the physics server, and returns the that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's normal direction and distance properties.

PhysicsServer3DExtension.desc: Provides virtual methods that can be overridden to create custom implementations.

register_server.desc: Register a implementation by passing a [param name] and a that returns a object.

set_default_server.desc: Set the default implementation to the one identified by [param name], if [param priority] is greater than the priority of the current default implementation.

PhysicsServer3DRenderingServerHandler.desc: A class used to provide [method PhysicsServer3DExtension._soft_body_update_rendering_server] with a rendering handler for soft bodies.

_set_aabb.desc: Called by the to set the bounding box for the .

_set_normal.desc: Called by the to set the normal for the vertex at the index specified by [param vertex_id]. Note: The [param normal] parameter used to be of type const void* prior to Godot 4.2.

_set_vertex.desc: Called by the to set the position for the vertex at the index specified by [param vertex_id]. Note: The [param vertex] parameter used to be of type const void* prior to Godot 4.2.

set_aabb.desc: Sets the bounding box for the .

set_normal.desc: Sets the normal for the vertex at the index specified by [param vertex_id].

set_vertex.desc: Sets the position for the vertex at the index specified by [param vertex_id].

PhysicsTestMotionResult2D.desc: Describes the motion and collision result from [method PhysicsServer2D.body_test_motion].

get_collider.desc: Returns the colliding body's attached , if a collision occurred.

get_collider_id.desc: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached , if a collision occurred. See [method Object.get_instance_id].

get_collider_rid.desc: Returns the colliding body's used by the , if a collision occurred.

get_collider_shape.desc: Returns the colliding body's shape index, if a collision occurred. See .

get_collider_velocity.desc: Returns the colliding body's velocity, if a collision occurred.

get_collision_depth.desc: Returns the length of overlap along the collision normal, if a collision occurred.

get_collision_local_shape.desc: Returns the moving object's colliding shape, if a collision occurred.

get_collision_normal.desc: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision, if a collision occurred.

get_collision_point.desc: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates, if a collision occurred.

get_collider.desc: Returns the colliding body's attached given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collider_id.desc: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred. See [method Object.get_instance_id].

get_collider_rid.desc: Returns the colliding body's used by the given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collider_shape.desc: Returns the colliding body's shape index given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred. See .

get_collider_velocity.desc: Returns the colliding body's velocity given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collision_count.desc: Returns the number of detected collisions.

get_collision_depth.desc: Returns the length of overlap along the collision normal given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collision_local_shape.desc: Returns the moving object's colliding shape given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collision_normal.desc: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_collision_point.desc: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates given a collision index (the deepest collision by default), if a collision occurred.

get_remainder.desc: Returns the moving object's remaining movement vector.

Plane.desc: A plane in Hessian normal form.

distance_to.desc: Returns the shortest distance from the plane to the position [param point]. If the point is above the plane, the distance will be positive. If below, the distance will be negative.

get_center.desc: Returns the center of the plane.

has_point.desc: Returns true if [param point] is inside the plane. Comparison uses a custom minimum [param tolerance] threshold.

intersect_3.desc: Returns the intersection point of the three planes [param b], [param c] and this plane. If no intersection is found, null is returned.

intersects_ray.desc: Returns the intersection point of a ray consisting of the position [param from] and the direction normal [param dir] with this plane. If no intersection is found, null is returned.

intersects_segment.desc: Returns the intersection point of a segment from position [param from] to position [param to] with this plane. If no intersection is found, null is returned.

is_equal_approx.desc: Returns true if this plane and [param to_plane] are approximately equal, by running [method @GlobalScope.is_equal_approx] on each component.

is_finite.desc: Returns true if this plane is finite, by calling [method @GlobalScope.is_finite] on each component.

is_point_over.desc: Returns true if [param point] is located above the plane.

normalized.desc: Returns a copy of the plane, with normalized [member normal] (so it's a unit vector). Returns Plane(0, 0, 0, 0) if [member normal] can't be normalized (it has zero length).

project.desc: Returns the orthogonal projection of [param point] into a point in the plane.

erase_bone.desc: Removes the specified bone from this .

get_bone_count.desc: Returns the number of bones in this .

is_point_inside.desc: Returns true if [param point] falls inside the polygon area. var polygon_path_finder = PolygonPathFinder.new() var points = [Vector2(0.0, 0.0), Vector2(1.0, 0.0), Vector2(0.0, 1.0)] var connections = [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0] polygon_path_finder.setup(points, connections) print(polygon_path_finder.is_point_inside(Vector2(0.2, 0.2))) # Prints true print(polygon_path_finder.is_point_inside(Vector2(1.0, 1.0))) # Prints false var polygonPathFinder = new PolygonPathFinder(); Vector2[] points = [ new Vector2(0.0f, 0.0f), new Vector2(1.0f, 0.0f), new Vector2(0.0f, 1.0f) ]; int[] connections = [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0]; polygonPathFinder.Setup(points, connections); GD.Print(polygonPathFinder.IsPointInside(new Vector2(0.2f, 0.2f))); // Prints True GD.Print(polygonPathFinder.IsPointInside(new Vector2(1.0f, 1.0f))); // Prints False

setup.desc: Sets up with an array of points that define the vertices of the polygon, and an array of indices that determine the edges of the polygon. The length of [param connections] must be even, returns an error if odd. var polygon_path_finder = PolygonPathFinder.new() var points = [Vector2(0.0, 0.0), Vector2(1.0, 0.0), Vector2(0.0, 1.0)] var connections = [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0] polygon_path_finder.setup(points, connections) var polygonPathFinder = new PolygonPathFinder(); Vector2[] points = [ new Vector2(0.0f, 0.0f), new Vector2(1.0f, 0.0f), new Vector2(0.0f, 1.0f) ]; int[] connections = [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0]; polygonPathFinder.Setup(points, connections);
